subject: Telemetry accreditation: SIEM ingest & trace hooks for Redwood Private
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmecorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Ops <security-ops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry accreditation: SIEM ingest and authz for Redwood Private

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — we're progressing on the SOC2 evidence collection and hit a couple of questions about telemetry for the Private deployment we need answers for the audit. Can you confirm the following points so we can include them in our control narrative?

- Supported egress patterns: do you support both Splunk HEC and syslog over TLS from the customer-side forwarder, or is one preferred for Private (VPC/on-prem) installs?
- Token scoping: can a single HEC token be scoped per-tenant and rotated independently? What does token rotation look like operationally?
- Trace hooks: how do you expose tracing context (W3C traceparent) when the runtime runs in customer VPC? Can we collect spans without adding sampling to customer apps?
- Evidence bundle: what artifacts can Redwood provide for retention / custody (e.g., delivery receipts, signed manifests, mapping of log streams to retention windows)?

I've attached our initial evidence checklist and a telemetry matrix (see attachments). We'd like to capture your answers in the next 48 hours if possible — the auditor will need the narrative and a sample config.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Senior InfoSec Manager, Acme Corp
security-ops@acme.com

Attachments: required-evidence-checklist.pdf, redwood-telemetry-matrix.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry accreditation: SIEM ingest and authz for Redwood Private

Hi Sarah — thanks for the checklist and the clear questions. Looping in Kimberly (security), Camila (solutions), and Marissa (observability PM) so we can give a consolidated answer. High-level answers inline below; we'll follow up with a short config sample and a Confluence design link.

- Supported egress patterns: Redwood Private supports both syslog (TLS) and Splunk HEC. For enterprise SIEMs we usually recommend HEC when the customer runs a managed Splunk instance (better metadata and deduplication), and syslog TLS when customers prefer existing log collectors. Both routes are first-class and supported by the forwarder in the on-prem package.

- Token scoping & rotation: HEC tokens can be scoped per-tenant and per-route; tokens are stored encrypted in the Private control plane. Rotation can be automated via the customer's KMS-backed key rotation schedule or performed manually; we provide a rotation CLI and a REST endpoint for token rollover that supports zero-downtime swap (we swap token endpoints and invalidate old tokens once mirrors confirm delivery).

- Trace hooks: the runtime emits W3C traceparent and baggage across RPC boundaries when instrumented. For Private deployments we surface a trace-forwarder that can emit sampled spans to a local collector (OTLP) without requiring app-level changes — we recommend the collector sidecar pattern so you can set sampling and redaction policies centrally.

- Evidence bundle: we can produce delivery receipts (timestamped manifests), signed metadata for each exported file (SHA256 + signature), and a mapping of streams to retention windows. We can also provide a small export (sample) containing anonymized records for auditor review.

We'll attach a minimal HEC configuration snippet and a sampling guide in the next message. If you like, we can schedule a 30-minute run-through tomorrow to walk through the Confluence design and export sample.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: telemetry-hec-sample.conf (coming), trace-sampling-guide.md (coming)

Thanks Vivek — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from the auditor and our Splunk team:

- Splunk-specific: we need token scoping to be able to restrict ingestion to specific index names and source types. Can you confirm the HEC integration allows enforcement of index/source_type at token level or via a proxy?
- Trace sampling: the auditor wants assurance that spans from user prompt/LLM invocation chains can be sampled and correlated with generated request IDs. Can your collector preserve the correlation id between the request/response and spans?
- Evidence format: we'd like the signed manifest to include file checksums and a statement of custody (who initiated export + timestamp). Can you provide an example manifest?

I've attached a small allowlist of Splunk endpoints we plan to use to validate connectivity and accepted ciphers.

Appreciate a short example config and a manifest sample. If possible, Kimberly and Camila on your side should be cc'd on the artifact so the auditor can ask clarifying questions directly.

Cheers,
Sarah

Attachments: splunk-hec-allowlist.txt

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmecorp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry accreditation: SIEM ingest and authz for Redwood Private

Hi Sarah — Kimberly here (Security Engineering). Apologies for the slightly delayed reply; I pulled together the artifacts the auditor asked for and a short checklist you can drop into your evidence repo. Key items attached.

1) HEC scoping: our forwarder supports per-token routing via a proxy pattern — tokens are associated with a routing rule that includes target index and source_type. The proxy enforces routing by validating token -> rule mapping on every connection. We can provide a deployment sample that pins token->index for your Splunk environment.

2) Token rotation: rotation can be orchestrated through the Private control plane API. We rotate tokens by: (a) create new token, (b) mirror traffic to new token for 5 minutes, (c) swap active pointer, (d) decommission old token after successful delivery confirmation. Logs for the rotation sequence are included in the evidence bundle.

3) Trace correlation: the runtime injects a correlation header (x-rw-request-id) alongside W3C traceparent. Our collector preserves both and includes both in span attributes so you can map an LLM request to the generated token/response. Sample OTLP export attached.

4) Manifest example: attached is manifest-example.json (SHA256 checksums + signer DN + timestamp + initiating user). We also include a short guidance doc on minimal redaction for exported samples.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded the sample HEC config and the manifest example to the Confluence page (link below).
- If you'd like a live handoff, I've booked a 30-minute slot with your calendar for Fri 13 Aug at 10:00 PDT — invite should appear (if time doesn't work, tell us preferred times).
